nodes.description: public pure recover(bytes32 hash, bytes memory signature): parses a 65-byte ECDSA signature in inline assembly, validates s-range and v, then calls ecrecover to return the signer address.
external pure toEthSignedMessageHash(bytes32 hash): wraps a hash with the Ethereum Signed Message prefix using keccak256(abi.encodePacked(...)).
ecrecover(hash, v, r, s) precompile call: can return address(0) on invalid signatures and is historically malleable; the recovered signer is a security-critical, attacker-influenceable value.
Inline assembly block reading signature via mload(add(signature,0x20/0x40/0x60)) and byte(0,...) into r, s, v without bounds/layout safety checks.
Parameter hash of recover(bytes32 hash, bytes memory signature).
Parameter signature (bytes memory) of recover: attacker-controllable raw signature bytes copied in memory.
Local bytes32 r: first 32 bytes of the supplied signature, extracted by assembly.
Local bytes32 s: second 32 bytes of the supplied signature, validated against the lower-half order bound.
Local uint8 v: recovery id extracted from the 65th byte, required to be 27 or 28.

edges.reason: recover reads the hash parameter used as the recovery digest.
recover reads the signature parameter and checks its length (65 bytes).
The signature memory buffer is read by the inline assembly to extract r, s and v.
Assembly assigns the first signature word into local r.
Assembly assigns the second signature word into local s.
Assembly assigns the 65th signature byte into local v.
recover executes the inline assembly block for signature parsing.
recover invokes the ecrecover precompile when length, s-range and v checks pass.
Local r is passed as an argument to ecrecover.
Local s is passed as an argument to ecrecover.
Local v is passed as an argument to ecrecover.
The hash parameter flows directly into ecrecover as the signed digest.
toEthSignedMessageHash reads its hash parameter and prefixes it.
